title: RL runs
description: One reinforcement-learning run, across every process that reports it. Runs are identified by run_id, which the MarinSkyRL driver, trainer and Ray controller all stamp. Accelerator and engine series carry no run_id of their own and are joined to the run through the nodes and the Iris job its own rows name. Everything here is read from telemetry_v1, so it answers after the run's pods are gone; W&B keeps the full-fidelity experiment record.

params.value: SELECT DISTINCT run_id AS value FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE service = 'marinskyrl' AND name = 'policy_step' AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND run_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Optimizer step and policy lag
panels.description: The trainer's optimizer step, and the newest policy version whose generated work was consumed in the same bucket. The vertical gap between them is the policy lag in optimizer steps: superimposed is on-policy, a widening gap is generation falling behind, and a gap pinned flat at max_staleness_steps is admission clamping and buying throughput with staleness. The upper line is a counter and only ever rises, so flat is the failure signal and down is impossible. This gap is MAX(policy_step) − MAX(weights_step) per bucket, a best-case estimate read by eye; the measured per-group distribution is the off-policy staleness panel two rows down.

defaults.noValue: No policy_step rows in this window. The run picker only offers runs that emitted one, so this means the trainer stopped — check the producers table to the right.

params.value: SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS t, 'trainer step · ' || execution_uid AS series, MAX(value) AS value FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE name = 'policy_step' AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1, execution_uid UNION ALL SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS t, 'producing policy · ' || execution_uid AS series, MAX(CAST(json_get(attributes_json, 'weights_step') AS DOUBLE)) AS value FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE name = 'work_completed' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'weights_step') IS NOT NULL AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1, execution_uid ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Rollouts, samples and tokens completed
panels.description: Work the trainer finished in each time bucket. A rollout is one completed trajectory; a sample is one generated response segment, so a multi-turn or step-wise rollout counts as several samples and only its terminal segment as a rollout. These arrive as native counter deltas and sum directly, so no line here is a running total, and generated tokens ÷ rollouts is mean trajectory length. Harbor counts trials under this same metric name and a trial is not a rollout; the trainer also emits a policy_step work kind here, separate from the policy_step gauge the panel to the left reads.

params.value: SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS t, SUM(CASE WHEN json_get(attributes_json, 'work_kind') = 'rollout' THEN value END) AS rollouts, SUM(CASE WHEN json_get(attributes_json, 'work_kind') = 'sample' THEN value END) AS samples, SUM(CASE WHEN json_get(attributes_json, 'work_kind') = 'generated_token' THEN value END) AS generated_tokens FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE service = 'marinskyrl' AND name = 'work_completed' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'work_kind') IN ('rollout', 'sample', 'generated_token') AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Producers reporting this run
panels.description: One row per service × role × metric source that stamped this run_id, and when each last reported. A healthy async run shows marinskyrl several times (driver, trainer, controller, plus a ray metric source), one vllm row covering every inference engine, and one harbor row as orchestrator; the Iris node agent never appears, because it is a fleet process that stamps no run_id. A producer that never called configure() fails silently — no exception, no log, lost_records stays 0 — so a missing row here is the only evidence you get.

defaults.noValue: No producers under this run_id in this window.

params.value: SELECT service AS producer, COALESCE(json_get(resource_attributes_json, 'role'), '') AS role, COALESCE(execution_uid, '') AS attempt, COALESCE(json_get(attributes_json, 'metric_source'), '') AS metric_source, COUNT(DISTINCT name) AS signals, COUNT(*) AS records, MAX(timestamp_ms) AS last_record_ms FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE 1=1 AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4 UNION ALL SELECT service AS producer, COALESCE(json_get(resource_attributes_json, 'role'), '') AS role, COALESCE(execution_uid, '') AS attempt, COALESCE(json_get(attributes_json, 'metric_source'), '') AS metric_source, COUNT(DISTINCT name) AS signals, COUNT(*) AS records, MAX(timestamp_ms) AS last_record_ms FROM "telemetry_v1.vllm" WHERE 1=1 AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4 UNION ALL SELECT service AS producer, COALESCE(json_get(resource_attributes_json, 'role'), '') AS role, COALESCE(execution_uid, '') AS attempt, COALESCE(json_get(attributes_json, 'metric_source'), '') AS metric_source, COUNT(DISTINCT name) AS signals, COUNT(*) AS records, MAX(timestamp_ms) AS last_record_ms FROM "telemetry_v1.harbor" WHERE 1=1 AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4

panels.title: Where did the wall clock go?
Optimizer step decomposition (exclusive time)
panels.description: Mean seconds each phase spent on its own work inside one optimizer step: the span's duration minus the spans it contains. Exclusive time is the only kind that may be stacked, because the bands then sum to the step. Checkpointing, eval and export are recorded alongside a step and contained by none, so the panel reads one root subtree rather than every exclusive span. Blank until the producer stamps root; until then the panel to the right is the two-way split.

defaults.noValue: No exclusive-clock rows carrying root='step'. This build does not stamp them yet -- read the critical-path panel to the right.

params.value: SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS t, json_get(attributes_json, 'phase') AS series, AVG(value) AS value FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE name = 'phase_duration_seconds' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'clock_domain') = 'exclusive' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'root') = 'step' AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Rollout wait vs train step (critical path)
panels.description: Mean seconds per optimizer step that the trainer blocked, split two ways: waiting for generated rollouts, and inside the optimizer step itself. Rollout wait dominating means the trainer is starved for generation rather than slow at training — read it against the rollout buffer below to see which side is holding the work. These spans are inclusive of everything they contain, so they say which half of the step is expensive and never what inside it; they must not be stacked. Each phase is split by outcome because a phase that raised recorded how long it ran before failing, which is not how long that phase takes.

params.value: SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS t, json_get(attributes_json, 'phase') || ' · ' || json_get(attributes_json, 'outcome') AS series, AVG(value) AS value FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE service = 'marinskyrl' AND name = 'phase_duration_seconds' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'clock_domain') = 'critical_path' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'phase') IN ('rollout_or_inference_wait', 'train_step') AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Rollout buffer occupancy (groups)
panels.description: Completed rollout groups sitting in the fully-async buffer, against the buffer's capacity. One group is one prompt's n samples, so this counts groups and not individual rollouts. Pinned at capacity means generation is ahead and the trainer is the bottleneck; near zero while the trainer waits is the reverse — the pair is the evidence for choosing an inference-to-training ratio, which our configs span from 0.5:1 to 6:1 with no recorded rationale. Async trainer only: one call site in fully_async_trainer.py, so a sync run is blank, and blank reads identically to starved.

defaults.noValue: No rollout-buffer rows. Sync trainer, or the buffer never reported — this is not a starved buffer.

params.value: SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS t, AVG(CASE WHEN name = 'rollout_queue_depth' THEN value END) AS depth, AVG(CASE WHEN name = 'rollout_capacity' THEN value END) AS capacity FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE service = 'marinskyrl' AND name IN ('rollout_queue_depth', 'rollout_capacity') AND json_get(attributes_json, 'queue') = 'rollout_buffer' AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: GPU utilization on this run's nodes
panels.description: Mean GPU busy percentage on the nodes this run occupied, from the Iris node agent. The node agent stamps no run_id and never will, so this is joined through node_name: each node is credited to whichever run reported most from it in that time bucket, and a node two runs share goes entirely to one of them. Read it against the critical-path panel — a long step with low GPU busy is stranded accelerator time.

defaults.noValue: No node join. Trainer rows carry no node_name, or the node agent is not reporting this cluster. This is never “GPUs idle”.

params.value: WITH raw AS ( SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') AS cl, date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS t, service, node_name AS node, run_id AS run, json_get(attributes_json, 'gpu_uuid') AS gpu, name, value FROM "telemetry_v1.node_agent" WHERE name = 'gpu_utilization_percent' AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) UNION ALL SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') AS cl, date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS t, service, node_name AS node, run_id AS run, NULL AS gpu, name, value FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE 1=1 AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) ), run_node AS ( SELECT cl, t, node, run FROM ( SELECT cl, t, node, run, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cl, t, node ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rn FROM raw WHERE service = 'marinskyrl' AND node <> '' GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4) WHERE rn = 1 ), gpu AS ( SELECT cl, t, node, gpu, AVG(value) AS utilization FROM raw WHERE service = 'iris-node-agent' GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4 ) SELECT gpu.t AS t, run_node.run AS series, AVG(gpu.utilization) AS value FROM gpu JOIN run_node ON gpu.cl = run_node.cl AND gpu.t = run_node.t AND gpu.node = run_node.node WHERE run_node.run IN (${run:sqlstring}) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Engine token throughput
panels.description: Prompt and generated tokens per second, summed across the run's inference engines and differenced per engine from cumulative counters. Read the ratio rather than either line: under GRPO all n samples of a group share one prompt, so a prompt-heavy ratio is the signal that prefix-cache routing would pay, and the prefix-cache panel below says whether the cache is already catching it. The generated line against generated tokens on the work-completed panel is the discard rate — generation the trainer never consumed.

defaults.noValue: No vLLM rows for this run. If the whole rank is blank, the engine exporter is down rather than six separate faults.

params.value: WITH samples AS ( SELECT timestamp_ms, name, attributes_json, value - LAG(value) OVER (PARTITION BY service, run_id, execution_uid, node_name, process_index, name, resource_attributes_json, attributes_json ORDER BY timestamp_ms, seq) AS delta FROM "telemetry_v1.vllm" WHERE name IN ('generation_tokens_total', 'prompt_tokens_total') AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) ) SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS t, SUM(CASE WHEN name = 'generation_tokens_total' THEN GREATEST(delta, 0) END) / (${__interval_ms} / 1000.0) AS generation, SUM(CASE WHEN name = 'prompt_tokens_total' THEN GREATEST(delta, 0) END) / (${__interval_ms} / 1000.0) AS prompt FROM samples WHERE delta IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Engine queue and KV-cache
panels.description: Requests running and requests queued at the inference engines, and how full their KV-cache is, each averaged across engines. Queued high with KV-cache low is a scheduling limit — add engines, or raise the concurrency cap. Both high is a genuine KV-cache limit, and the preemptions panel below says whether it cost anything. Neither number separates the two cases alone.

defaults.noValue: No vLLM rows for this run. If the whole rank is blank, the engine exporter is down rather than six separate faults.

params.value: SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS t, AVG(CASE WHEN name = 'num_requests_running' THEN value END) AS running, AVG(CASE WHEN name = 'num_requests_waiting' THEN value END) AS waiting, AVG(CASE WHEN name = 'kv_cache_usage_perc' THEN value END) AS kv_cache FROM "telemetry_v1.vllm" WHERE name IN ('num_requests_running', 'num_requests_waiting', 'kv_cache_usage_perc') AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Engine request latency (mean by stage)
panels.description: Mean seconds per finished request at each stage: queue, prefill, decode, time to first token, and end to end. The forwarder ships Prometheus histograms as _sum and _count, so this is Σ(Δ_sum) ÷ Σ(Δ_count) over each time bucket — a mean, which cannot show a tail. The straggler panel below carries that reading. End to end and time to first token contain the other stages, so these series neither stack nor sum.

defaults.noValue: No vLLM rows for this run. If the whole rank is blank, the engine exporter is down rather than six separate faults.

params.value: WITH samples AS ( SELECT timestamp_ms, name, attributes_json, value - LAG(value) OVER (PARTITION BY service, run_id, execution_uid, node_name, process_index, name, resource_attributes_json, attributes_json ORDER BY timestamp_ms, seq) AS delta FROM "telemetry_v1.vllm" WHERE (name LIKE '%_seconds_sum' OR name LIKE '%_seconds_count') AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) ) SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS t, replace(replace(name, '_sum', ''), '_count', '') AS series, SUM(CASE WHEN name LIKE '%_sum' THEN GREATEST(delta, 0) END) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN name LIKE '%_count' THEN GREATEST(delta, 0) END), 0) AS value FROM samples WHERE delta IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Prefix-cache hit rate
panels.description: Cached prompt tokens ÷ queried prompt tokens across the run's inference engines, from two counters. Both counters are in tokens, so this is not the share of requests that hit. It is the evidence base for cache-aware routing: under GRPO all n samples of a group share one prompt, so the reachable ceiling is high and the gap to it is the opportunity. Read it under engine throughput — a prompt-heavy throughput ratio with a low hit rate is prefill being paid for repeatedly.

defaults.noValue: No vLLM rows for this run. If the whole rank is blank, the engine exporter is down rather than six separate faults.

params.value: WITH d AS ( SELECT timestamp_ms, name, value - LAG(value) OVER (PARTITION BY service, run_id, execution_uid, node_name, process_index, name, resource_attributes_json, attributes_json ORDER BY timestamp_ms, seq) AS delta FROM "telemetry_v1.vllm" WHERE name IN ('prefix_cache_hits_total', 'prefix_cache_queries_total') AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) ) SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS t, 'hit rate' AS series, SUM(CASE WHEN name = 'prefix_cache_hits_total' THEN GREATEST(delta, 0) END) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN name = 'prefix_cache_queries_total' THEN GREATEST(delta, 0) END), 0) AS value FROM d WHERE delta IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Engine KV-cache preemptions
panels.description: Requests the inference engine evicted from its KV-cache and had to recompute, per time bucket, differenced from a cumulative counter. This is vLLM's own scheduler preemption and is unrelated to Kubernetes pod preemption or Iris job preemption. A counter cannot miss an event between scrapes the way a KV-cache high-water gauge can, so this is the only panel showing KV-cache pressure that actually cost something: high KV-cache use above with zero here cost nothing.

defaults.noValue: No vLLM rows for this run. If the whole rank is blank, the engine exporter is down rather than six separate faults.

params.value: WITH d AS ( SELECT timestamp_ms, value - LAG(value) OVER (PARTITION BY service, run_id, execution_uid, node_name, process_index, name, resource_attributes_json, attributes_json ORDER BY timestamp_ms, seq) AS delta FROM "telemetry_v1.vllm" WHERE name = 'num_preemptions_total' AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) ) SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS t, 'preemptions' AS series, SUM(GREATEST(delta, 0)) AS value FROM d WHERE delta IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Straggler proxy: rollout wait p99 ÷ p50
panels.description: The 99th percentile of the trainer's critical-path rollout wait divided by its median, over the rows in each time bucket. One row is one optimizer step, so this measures step-to-step spread and stands in for the straggler tax rather than measuring it; the per-rollout distribution needs a per-rollout record, which no producer emits. Above about 2 the tail is multiplying every synchronous step — pair it with effective batch size after filtering, because taking the first n completions fills early batches with short, easy tasks. The ratio only means anything when a bucket holds many steps: at the default window the bucket is under a minute while a step is minutes, so raise the panel's minimum interval to 30m before reading it.

params.value: SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS t, 'p99 / p50' AS series, approx_percentile_cont(value, 0.99) / NULLIF(approx_percentile_cont(value, 0.5), 0) AS value FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE name = 'phase_duration_seconds' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'clock_domain') = 'critical_path' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'phase') = 'rollout_or_inference_wait' AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Is it learning, and can the reward be trusted?
Off-policy staleness (optimizer steps behind)
panels.description: How many optimizer steps old each admitted group's policy was when the trainer consumed it, measured at admission, one observation per group. The producer cannot compute this, because a group can wait in the buffer across step boundaries and so cannot know which step will consume it. Staleness as a logged number, at the k≈4–8 the async trainer targets; it is also the input any off-policy correction needs. Watch p99: the trainer asserts max staleness ≤ max_staleness_steps immediately after recording, so a p99 climbing toward the configured max is the last thing you see before the run aborts. Async trainer only — a sync run is on-policy by construction.

defaults.noValue: No staleness rows. Async trainer only; a sync run is on-policy by construction.

params.value: SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS t, 'p50' AS series, approx_percentile_cont(value, 0.5) AS value FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE name = 'rollout_staleness_steps' AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1, 2 UNION ALL SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS t, 'p99' AS series, approx_percentile_cont(value, 0.99) AS value FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE name = 'rollout_staleness_steps' AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Why engine requests finished
panels.description: Finished inference-engine requests per time bucket, split by vLLM's finished_reason. The set is open — stop, length, abort, error and repetition on the pinned build — so read whatever appears rather than expecting three. A rising length share is truncation quietly corrupting the reward signal: the model was cut off rather than choosing to stop, and the verifier scores the truncation anyway. These count engine requests, so one rollout is several of them when the group is sampled n ways or the task is multi-turn.

params.value: WITH d AS ( SELECT timestamp_ms, attributes_json, value - LAG(value) OVER (PARTITION BY service, run_id, execution_uid, node_name, process_index, name, resource_attributes_json, attributes_json ORDER BY timestamp_ms, seq) AS delta FROM "telemetry_v1.vllm" WHERE name = 'request_success_total' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'finished_reason') IS NOT NULL AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) ) SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS t, json_get(attributes_json, 'finished_reason') AS series, SUM(GREATEST(delta, 0)) AS value FROM d WHERE delta IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Ray object store occupancy
panels.description: Share of the Ray object store in use across the run's nodes: used ÷ (used + free), so it does not move when the node count does. Climbing toward 1 is the store about to spill, and spill surfaces as rollout latency long before it surfaces as a failure. This is Ray plumbing and is unrelated to the engines' KV-cache.

defaults.noValue: No Ray rows for this run. Non-Ray deployment, or the Ray metric bridge is off.

params.value: SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS t, SUM(CASE WHEN name = 'ray_object_store_used_memory' THEN value END) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN name IN ('ray_object_store_used_memory', 'ray_object_store_available_memory') THEN value END), 0) AS object_store_used_fraction FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE service = 'marinskyrl' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'metric_source') = 'ray' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'source_temporality') = 'current_snapshot' AND name IN ('ray_object_store_used_memory', 'ray_object_store_available_memory') AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Ray spill manager bytes by state
panels.description: Bytes the Ray spill manager is tracking, split by its own state label, averaged per node. Read the states separately and never together: pinned, pending spill and pending restore are current occupancy, while spilled and restored are lifetime running totals that only ever climb. A pending-spill line that stops draining is the plumbing failing; a spilled line whose slope steepens is trajectories bigger than budgeted.

defaults.noValue: No Ray rows for this run. Non-Ray deployment, or the Ray metric bridge is off.

params.value: SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS t, COALESCE(json_get(attributes_json, 'state'), 'unlabelled') AS series, AVG(value) AS value FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE service = 'marinskyrl' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'metric_source') = 'ray' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'source_temporality') = 'current_snapshot' AND name = 'ray_spill_manager_objects_bytes' AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1
